title: Find Beautiful Indices in the Given Array I
summary: Given a string s and strings a, b, and an integer k, find indices i where s[i:i+len(a)] equals a, s[j:j+len(b)] equals b, and |j - i| is at most k.
statement: Given a string s and strings a, b, and an integer k, find indices i where s[i:i+len(a)] equals a, s[j:j+len(b)] equals b, and |j - i| is at most k. Return these indices in ascending order.
constraints: s, a, and b are lowercase strings; a and b have length at most ten; k is nonnegative.
Index i must start an occurrence of a and lie within k positions of some start of b.
Return all qualifying a-start indices in ascending order.
reference_solution:
def beautiful_indices_small(s,a,b,k):
    first=[index for index in range(len(s)-len(a)+1) if s.startswith(a,index)]
    second=[index for index in range(len(s)-len(b)+1) if s.startswith(b,index)]
    return [index for index in first if any(abs(index-other)<=k for other in second)]

hints: Occurrence starts can be enumerated directly because the short patterns bound each comparison.
Collect every start of a and b, then retain a starts having any b start within k.
Use startswith at each legal start; for each a index test abs(i-j)<=k over b starts.
The occurrence lists contain exactly all possible witnesses, and the direct distance test matches the definition.

tests.explanation: The my occurrences at sixteen and thirty-three are within fifteen start positions of squirrel occurrences at four and eighteen.
The shared occurrence at index zero witnesses its own distance zero, so zero is beautiful.
